questions.text: Grid Extension Risk & Interface: Interaction with national grid: (1) Grid arrival risk (what if grid reaches off-grid customer?); (2) Grid reliability (is grid a competitor or backup?); (3) Interconnection potential (can mini-grid connect to main grid?); (4) Compensation policy (if grid arrives); (5) Grid compatibility (voltage/frequency); (6) Hybrid opportunities; (7) Policy on exclusivity zones.
questions.evidence_required: Grid expansion plans, Exclusivity agreements, Interconnection technical standards, Compensation regulations
questions.africa_specific_notes: Grid arrival is #1 risk for mini-grids. 'Grid is coming' rumors stop sales. Grid often unreliable, so solar remains relevant as backup.

questions.text: Mobile Network Dependency: Reliance on telco infrastructure: (1) 2G/3G coverage at user locations; (2) SMS/USSD reliability; (3) Mobile money uptime; (4) IoT data connectivity; (5) SIM card management (M2M SIMs); (6) Telco partnerships; (7) Offline fallback capabilities.
questions.evidence_required: Coverage maps, Connectivity logs, SLA with telcos, Offline protocols
questions.africa_specific_notes: PAYG dead without network. IoT monitoring needs data. M2M SIM management complex across borders.

questions.text: Logistics & Transport Infrastructure: Moving hardware: (1) Port efficiency (clearing times); (2) Road quality (last-mile damage risk); (3) Rainy season accessibility; (4) Warehousing availability; (5) Transport costs; (6) Security during transport; (7) Reverse logistics capacity.
questions.evidence_required: Logistics plan, Clearing time data, Transport cost analysis, Insurance claims
questions.africa_specific_notes: Poor roads damage panels. Rainy season cuts off villages. Port delays cause stockouts.

questions.text: National Energy Policy & Targets: Alignment with government: (1) Electrification targets (universal access by 2030?); (2) Off-grid strategy (is it recognized?); (3) Integrated National Energy Plan; (4) Subsidy policy (Kerosene subsidies? Solar subsidies?); (5) VAT/Duty exemptions (consistency?); (6) Political support; (7) Policy stability.
questions.evidence_required: National energy policy docs, Gazette notices (VAT/Duty), Electrification plans
questions.africa_specific_notes: VAT/Duty exemptions often change overnight. Clear off-grid strategy essential for investment. Kerosene subsidies distort market.

questions.text: Mini-Grid Regulatory Framework: Specific mini-grid rules: (1) Licensing tiers (simplified for small grids?); (2) Tariff setting rules (cost-reflective?); (3) Technical standards; (4) Arrival of grid rules; (5) Subsidy frameworks; (6) Concession zones; (7) Approval timelines.
questions.evidence_required: Mini-grid regulations, Tariff guidelines, Licensing procedures
questions.africa_specific_notes: Cost-reflective tariffs often politically difficult. Licensing can take years. Clear 'arrival of grid' rules needed for bankability.

questions.text: E-Waste & Environmental Regulation: Environmental rules: (1) E-waste management laws; (2) Battery disposal regulations; (3) Producer responsibility (EPR); (4) Environmental impact assessment (EIA) requirements; (5) Carbon credit frameworks; (6) Enforcement levels; (7) Recycling infrastructure support.
questions.evidence_required: E-waste laws, EIA regulations, EPR guidelines
questions.africa_specific_notes: E-waste laws emerging but enforcement weak. EPR (Extended Producer Responsibility) becoming standard.

questions.text: Distribution & Sales Ecosystem: Last-mile reach: (1) Agent network density; (2) Partnership models (MFIs, Co-ops, Telcos); (3) Retail partnerships; (4) Community based organizations; (5) Last-mile logistics partners; (6) Marketing channels; (7) Trust networks.
questions.evidence_required: Distribution map, Partnership contracts, Agent list
questions.africa_specific_notes: Partnerships (e.g., with cocoa co-ops, dairy unions) lower CAC. Trust networks essential for sales.

questions.text: Financial Ecosystem Support: Access to finance: (1) Local bank lending to sector; (2) Microfinance availability for users; (3) Forex availability; (4) Mobile money liquidity; (5) Credit bureau coverage; (6) Investor landscape; (7) Grant/RBF availability.
questions.evidence_required: Loan products, Forex availability data, Credit bureau reports
questions.africa_specific_notes: Local debt hard to get (high interest). Forex scarcity (e.g., Ethiopia, Nigeria) is a major blocker. End-user finance (MFIs) boosts affordability.

questions.text: Industry Association & Advocacy: Collective action: (1) National renewable energy association strength; (2) GOGLA engagement; (3) Public-private dialogue; (4) Data sharing; (5) Standards adoption; (6) Joint advocacy (e.g., on VAT); (7) Code of conduct enforcement.
questions.evidence_required: Association membership, Advocacy position papers, Meeting minutes
questions.africa_specific_notes: Strong associations (e.g., KEREA, USEA) critical for policy advocacy. Fragmented sector ignored by government.

questions.text: Productive Use Appliance Ecosystem: Availability of income-generating assets: (1) Appliance supply chain (availability of solar mills, pumps, fridges); (2) Appliance financing (asset finance for machines); (3) Maintenance services for appliances; (4) Market linkage (selling the produce); (5) Training on appliance use; (6) Quality standards for PUE appliances; (7) Bundling with energy service.
questions.evidence_required: Appliance catalog, Financing terms, Maintenance contracts
questions.africa_specific_notes: Energy is useless for income without the appliance. Supply chain for solar fridges/mills is weak.

questions.text: Community Acceptance & Trust: Social license: (1) Perception of solar (past bad experiences?); (2) Trust in agents; (3) Community leader support; (4) Cultural alignment; (5) Theft/vandalism risk; (6) Willingness to pay; (7) Understanding of 'service' vs 'ownership'.
questions.evidence_required: Community surveys, Leader endorsements, Vandalism reports
questions.africa_specific_notes: Market spoiled by cheap counterfeits ('solar doesn't work'). Trust must be rebuilt. Service model (PAYG) often confused with ownership.

questions.text: Productive Use & Economic Context: Economic integration: (1) Income seasonality (harvests); (2) Productive use opportunities (irrigation, cooling); (3) Market access for local produce; (4) Local economy vibrancy; (5) Skill levels; (6) Gender roles in economy; (7) Displacement effects.
questions.evidence_required: Economic assessment, Seasonality calendars, Value chain analysis
questions.africa_specific_notes: Farmers pay when they harvest (seasonality). PUE (Productive Use) drives income to pay for energy.

questions.text: Gender & Social Dynamics: Social inclusion: (1) Women's decision making power; (2) Female headed households; (3) Youth employment; (4) Marginalized groups; (5) Intra-household conflict (over light usage); (6) Safety benefits; (7) Health benefits.
questions.africa_specific_notes: Women benefit most (health, safety, chores). Youth often early adopters. Light reduces snake bites/fires.

questions.text: Affordability & Tiered Access: Reaching the poor: (1) Entry-level product affordability; (2) Flexible payment terms; (3) Subsidies for poorest; (4) Credit scoring inclusion; (5) Cost per kWh comparison; (6) Deposit barriers; (7) Reaching 'last mile'.
questions.evidence_required: Pricing analysis, Affordability studies, Subsidy data
questions.africa_specific_notes: Deposit is the biggest barrier. Daily payments match irregular income. Subsidies needed for ultra-poor.

questions.text: Geographic Equity: Serving remote areas: (1) Urban vs rural coverage; (2) Service quality in remote areas; (3) Logistics cost equalization; (4) Maintenance access in deep rural; (5) Network coverage in remote areas; (6) Island/mountain access; (7) Conflict zone access.
questions.evidence_required: Coverage maps, Service logs by region
questions.africa_specific_notes: Companies cherry-pick peri-urban areas. Deep rural left behind. Logistics costs drive inequality.

questions.text: Vulnerable Group Inclusion: Specific groups: (1) Refugees/IDPs; (2) Disabled persons; (3) Elderly; (4) Female-headed households; (5) Child-headed households; (6) Ethnic minorities; (7) Illiterate users.
questions.africa_specific_notes: Refugees often pay more for energy (diesel/candles). ID requirements block access. Accessibility features needed.

questions.text: Climate Resilience: Adapting to climate change: (1) Extreme weather resilience; (2) Impact of drought on hydro (if mini-grid); (3) Impact of cloud cover changes; (4) Flood risk to infrastructure; (5) Heat impact on efficiency; (6) Climate adaptation role of energy; (7) Disaster recovery.
questions.africa_specific_notes: Climate change increasing extreme weather. Hydro mini-grids fail in drought. Solar helps pumping (adaptation).

questions.text: Carbon & Pollution Impact: Environmental benefits: (1) Kerosene displacement; (2) Diesel displacement; (3) Carbon credits generation; (4) Indoor air quality improvement; (5) Deforestation reduction (less charcoal?); (6) Lifecycle emissions; (7) Black carbon reduction.
questions.africa_specific_notes: Kerosene/candles cause fires and lung disease. Diesel expensive and polluting. Carbon credits becoming revenue stream.

scoring_notes: Layer 6 (Ecosystem) for Energy in SSA: Grid extension risk and regulatory environment are existential factors. Mobile network dependency is absolute for PAYG. Last-mile distribution and affordability determine who gets access.
